dialogue_quality_notes: Participants spoke concisely and directly about needs and actions (e.g., requests and offers to move the drying rack).
Actions in the environment (moving rack, turning on extractor, washing utensils) quickly grounded verbal requests.
Little needless repetition; John repeated the ventilation request but it prompted action rather than empty agreement.
Roles and physical states remained consistent with env updates (who is at stove, extractor state, laundry protection).
evaluation.final_reason: Michelle turned on the extractor and washed shared utensils (Round 4), resolving the immediate smell and utensil issues; later verbal agreement to ventilate when cooking (Round 6) reinforces the practical settlement.
position_change_notes: Michelle: initially cooking and not running extractor; later agreed to run extractor and washed shared utensils (Turn 7 and env updates) — softened position via action.
John: raised ventilation concern twice (Rounds 1 and 6) and prompted practical responses rather than escalatory demands.
Fatimah: requested clarification about personal utensils (Round 2), then labeled her items and later agreed to the ventilation practice (Round 6) — moved from uncertainty to compliance.
Arjun: offered extractor/window when taking the stove (Round 3) and began cooking; he did not oppose ventilation and did not change a contentious position.

round_scores.evidence: John requests extractor or window while Michelle is cooking (Turn 2). Michelle has not yet responded; extractor=off and window initially closed. John moves the drying rack to allow window opening (env update). A preference conflict (ventilation vs current cooking state/weather concerns) is introduced but not contested.

Fatimah asks which utensils are personal and Michelle says to label and promises to wash and release the stove (Turns 3–4). Michelle releases the stove (env update). John's earlier ventilation request remains unaddressed; extractor still off and window closed.

Arjun takes the stove and offers to turn on extractor/open window if wanted (Turn 6). Fatimah labels utensils (env update). Extractor remains off and window closed; John's ventilation preference remains unresolved.

Michelle says she'll turn on the extractor and wash shared utensils (Turn 7); John asks that she keep it on until smell fades (Turn 8). Michelle turns on extractor and washes utensils (env updates). The immediate ventilation and shared-utensils issues are addressed by action.
Extractor is on and aroma is fading (env update). Shared utensils are clean and personal utensils labeled; Fatimah and Arjun begin prepping (Turns 10–11). No substantive disagreement is expressed.

John restates a request to agree to run extractor/open window for strong-smelling food (Turn 13); Fatimah agrees and commits to run extractor or open window when possible (Turn 14). Agreement is reached and no opposing position is voiced.

substantive_insights: Main tension was between ventilating (to remove smell) and protecting laundry from rain when opening the window; moving the drying rack removed that constraint.
Immediate practical actions (moving rack, turning on extractor, washing utensils, labeling) were effective at resolving the issues faster than abstract negotiation would have been.
The parties distinguished between solving the immediate problem (turn extractor on) and creating a future norm (agree to ventilate), and both were addressed.
Labeling/identification of personal utensils removed uncertainty about shared vs personal items and enabled prep to proceed without conflict.
